intents.message: Our volunteer coordinator flagged that the intake tool might be skewing against non-English speakers. intents.message: Last Thursday our intake chatbot told a Spanish-speaking caller she was not eligible for the food program when she was. It already went out, so testing the model for disparate impact is beside the point right now; I need a standing procedure for the next time one of these lands.
intents.label: right skill

intents.message: Our board chair wants AI failures on the agenda after the summarizer invented a quote from our executive director that went out in a newsletter. intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour board-agenda-reporting-builder is wrong because the board framing is only the occasion, and the requested artefact, named late, is the containment-to-review procedure for AI failures rather than a meeting agenda or packet.

intents.message: We run a small foundation and we built a tool that ranks incoming applications by likely impact. Everyone assumes the question is how mature our AI practices are, but what I actually need to know is whether that ranking pushes rural and immigrant-led applicants down.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour grantee-responsible-ai-due-diligence-scorecard is wrong because the funder is not scoring any applicant's AI maturity - it is testing its own ranking tool for unequal outcomes across applicant groups.

intents.message: Our microgrant queue is sorted by an automated score and lately the same three zip codes take everything. Before I touch the pipeline dashboard I want someone to actually run the numbers on whether that scoring treats applicants from the poorer neighbourhoods differently.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour grant-pipeline-lifecycle-tracker is wrong because the user defers pipeline work and asks for an outcome comparison across geographic and economic groups produced by one automated scoring process.

intents.message: The building purchase goes to our governance committee on the 14th. I don't need the analysis — I need the session itself laid out: minutes per item, who speaks when, the wording of what they'll be asked to approve, and whether we'll have enough directors present to carry it.

intents.why: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because the user rules out the reasoning and asks only for the mechanics of the sitting that will take the decision — running order, motion wording and quorum.

intents.message: We've got the governing body together on the 3rd for the first time since spring — last time I just sent round a written recap and it landed badly. Give me the running order, who presents each piece, how long each gets, and which items are for a decision rather than information.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour stakeholder-update-generator is wrong because nothing is being tailored for several audiences — this is one governance sitting needing an ordered, timed structure that separates decision items from information items.

intents.message: We can keep the current donor database, move to the platform our consultant likes, or fold it all into the church management system we already pay for. Both outside tools cleared our AI and data checks months ago — I just want the three routes weighed and a recommendation.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour responsible-ai-procurement-checklist is wrong because the vendor vetting is already finished and the remaining ask is a three-way comparison with a recommendation, one option of which is buying nothing at all.

intents.message: Our fiscal sponsor has been fine and that arrangement isn't what's bothering me. The real question is whether we take the state contract at all — it doubles our staff and ties us in for four years. Lay out the ways forward and pick one.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour fiscal-sponsorship-entity-advisor is wrong because the sponsorship is named only to be excluded, leaving a general commitment question that wants options and a pick.

intents.message: Our board chair also runs the consultancy we're about to contract with, and the auditor wants something in writing about how we're handling it. Draft me the memo — the relationship, why it's defensible, the safeguards. Our next meeting isn't until March.

intents.message: Our training arm now earns most of its income from course fees, and the accountant muttered something about our public support test being at risk. Do we spin the earned side out into its own company, or is there a cleaner way to hold both?

intents.label: right skill

intents.message: Good news, the Aldridge Trust liked our short version and asked for the long form by the 30th. Everything else in my funding folder can wait; I want the workplan and the evaluation piece written out for this one.
intents.label: right skill

intents.message: Where did we land with Kresge, did we ever send them anything? And while you're in there, lay out every other funder we have in flight by which stage it sits at and what closes soonest.

intents.message: The board meets Thursday and they will ask about money, but before I put anything in front of them I want my own list: every application in flight, what stage each is at, and what I have let slip past due on my side.

intents.message: Half our portfolio organizations now run AI somewhere in their intake process. Before the next board docket I want a comparable maturity read across all of them on oversight, data handling and safeguarding, so we can see which ones need capacity support from us.

intents.message: We are adding a question to next year's application about how organizations handle machine-learning tools that touch beneficiary data. intents.label: right skill

intents.message: A vendor pitched us their AI intake assistant and instead of buying it we ended up building our own version, Frontdesk. Now our biggest institutional partner wants it written up against the four-function risk framework before they'll integrate with us. What would that look like?

intents.why: Nearest neighbour responsible-ai-procurement-checklist is wrong because the vendor pitch was declined and the system to be documented is one the organisation built itself, making this outbound single-system framework mapping rather than buyer-side vetting.

intents.message: Three partners keep asking about the same tool, our volunteer-vetting model. I don't want three differently pitched notes - I want one write-up mapping that model to all four functions of the risk framework reviewers recognise.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour stakeholder-update-generator is wrong because the user explicitly rejects audience-tailored versions and wants a single four-function framework mapping of one named model.

intents.message: A fundraising platform we are considering had a public failure last year where its AI drafted a donation appeal around a statistic it invented. We have not signed anything yet, so how do I press them on that before we do?
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour ai-incident-response-playbook-builder is wrong because the failure happened at a vendor the speaker has not yet bought from, and the ask is how to interrogate that vendor pre-signature rather than how to handle a future incident of their own.

intents.message: The AI transcription supplier we are about to sign with sent over a twelve-page conformance memo laid out against the four federal risk functions. I do not need one of those written from our side, I need to know which of their claims in it are red flags before I sign.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour nist-ai-rmf-crosswalk-generator is wrong because the speaker declines to author a crosswalk for their own system and, late in the request, asks how to read a supplier's claims for red flags ahead of signature.

intents.message: Our intake chatbot gave a family the wrong shelter address last week. We already fixed it and we already have a runbook for this kind of thing, so what I need now is the version for our board, the version for the two funders, and the version for frontline staff.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour ai-incident-response-playbook-builder is wrong because the standing process already exists and the remaining need is three audience-calibrated tellings of what happened.

intents.message: This month's numbers need to reach three sets of eyes: the trustees get a page ahead of their sitting, the partner churches get three lines for their bulletin, and my staff get the whole thing. Same facts, three lengths - write each one.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour board-agenda-reporting-builder is wrong because the trustee page is one of three differently sized renderings prepared ahead of a sitting, not the packet of motions, financials and quorum handling that would constitute the sitting itself.

intents.message: A funder asked whether we follow the federal AI risk framework. Before I answer I want an honest scored read across everything - oversight, documentation, data handling, how we'd cope with a failure - since we run about a dozen AI tools and no single one is the question.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour nist-ai-rmf-crosswalk-generator is wrong because the framework reference is only the prompt for the ask, while the request itself names no single system and demands a scored read spanning every governance dimension at once.

intents.message: We're a small family foundation and we've started leaning on AI inside our own grantmaking workflow. Someone suggested we score this the way we'd score a grantee, but I need it turned inward - how does our own house rate across the governance dimensions?
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour grantee-responsible-ai-due-diligence-scorecard is wrong because the funder is deliberately pointing the assessment at its own internal AI use rather than at any grantee's.

intents.message: We already signed up for three AI tools last year without much thought - one of them we barely use - and now they're baked into our case notes and donor letters. I don't need help picking a vendor, I need someone to grade how badly we're running what we already have.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour responsible-ai-procurement-checklist is wrong because the purchase already happened and the tools are in production, so the ask is a maturity read on deployed systems rather than pre-purchase vendor vetting.

intents.message: Last quarter our AI assistant leaked a client's address in a mass email and we handled it - the containment steps and the apology all went out fine. What I want now, and this is the part I keep putting off, is a scored read on every dimension of how we run AI, not another response plan.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour ai-incident-response-playbook-builder is wrong because the incident is already closed out and the late clause rejects a further response plan in favour of a scored read across every governance dimension.

intents.message: We have nothing written down about staff using AI. Can you draft us an actual acceptable-use policy from scratch - which tools are allowed, what data can never go into them, who signs off on exceptions - something I can drop straight into the staff handbook?
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: No skill in the set drafts governing policy text from scratch - the assessor explicitly disclaims policy drafting and hands it to a policy builder that is absent from these twelve, and every other skill assesses, scores, tracks, or reports rather than authoring an internal rule set.

intents.message: We just finished a maturity review of every AI tool we run and the weakest score by far was what happens when something goes wrong. Do not re-score us. Write the actual step-by-step for who gets called, how we rank how bad it is, and what we tell the family affected.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour ai-governance-assessor is wrong because the scoring pass is already done and the speaker explicitly refuses another one, asking instead for the standing response procedure that closes the identified gap.

intents.message: When our AI scheduling assistant leaked two clients' phone numbers into the wrong thread, I improvised notes to the clients, the board and our main funder in one afternoon. I never want to improvise that again, so turn the whole sequence into a documented process with severity levels.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour stakeholder-update-generator is wrong because the multi-audience notes are the past improvisation being replaced, and the deliverable named late in the request is a documented severity-tiered process.

intents.message: Our donor CRM's AI assistant was down for eleven hours during the year-end campaign and nobody knew who was supposed to decide whether to keep sending appeals by hand. We are staying with the supplier; I just want the internal steps we follow the next time a tool like this drops out.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour responsible-ai-procurement-checklist is wrong because the speaker rules out re-evaluating the supplier and wants internal containment and decision steps for a future outage of a critical AI-dependent workflow.

intents.message: Our conformance memo flagged that we have nothing written down for the moment one of our models produces something harmful. Rather than redo the mapping, I want the document that tells a staffer at nine at night who to call, how bad it counts as, and how we tell the person harmed.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour nist-ai-rmf-crosswalk-generator is wrong because the speaker declines to redo a framework mapping and asks for the operational runbook content, triage, severity and disclosure, that the memo found missing.

intents.message: A volunteer clicked a phishing link last week and someone used our payroll portal to reroute two staff direct deposits. What do we need to do now to lock the account down and meet our reporting obligations?
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: No skill in the set claims this because it is a conventional payroll-fraud and phishing incident with no AI system involved, and the library's incident skill is scoped exclusively to AI failures and harms.

intents.message: Our scholarship shortlisting model has been running a year now. Applicants who declare a disability seem to drop out at the shortlist step far more often than everyone else - can you work out whether that gap is real and what we should document about it?
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour ai-governance-assessor is wrong because the ask is an outcome-rate comparison on one named shortlisting model against a protected attribute, not a read on whether fairness practices exist anywhere.

intents.message: My data guy says we have to pick between equal selection rates and equal error rates for the housing waitlist model, and I honestly don't know how to choose. Can you work that through on the actual model and show me which groups come out worse under each option?
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because the choice is specifically between fairness metrics and must be settled by running them on one named waitlist model to see which groups fare worse, not by a general options-and-tradeoffs brief.

intents.message: We licensed a resume-screening product last spring - the vendor due diligence was done back then and the contract is signed. Six months of our own hiring data later, I want it checked against our applicants: are women and older candidates advancing at lower rates through it?
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour responsible-ai-procurement-checklist is wrong because the purchase and vendor check are finished, and the ask is an outcome-rate test of the live screener on the organisation's own applicants by gender and age.

intents.message: Somebody on staff complained that the food-pantry eligibility tool turned a family away unfairly, and yes, we logged it and apologised already. The complaint is one case though - what I want is that tool run against our whole year of decisions to see if Spanish-speaking households come out worse.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour ai-incident-response-playbook-builder is wrong because the single complaint is already handled and the late clause asks for a population-level outcome comparison on one named eligibility tool by language group.

intents.why: No skill in the set produces recruiting artefacts - job descriptions, interview rubrics and compensation bands are HR work, and the AI subject matter of the role does not turn the request into an assessment, a fairness test, or a board packet.

intents.why: Nearest neighbour grant-pipeline-lifecycle-tracker is wrong because funding is merely the subject matter of a meeting whose structure — timings, owners, pre-reads and a sign-off item — is the actual deliverable.

intents.message: One of our directors owns the firm we're about to sign a lease with. How do I sequence Tuesday's meeting so her stepping out is on the record and the rest still have the numbers to carry the vote?
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour fiscal-sponsorship-entity-advisor is wrong because the user is not asking whether the dual role is defensible or for anything in writing, only how to order the meeting so the recusal is minuted and the remaining directors still make quorum.

intents.message: Our exec committee is chewing over whether to merge the two program teams and everyone has a view. Before we get there, map the ninety minutes for me — order, owners, and the exact wording of what they'll be asked to adopt at the end.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because the merger question is only the topic; the late detail asks for the time map and the resolution wording, which is the meeting's structure rather than the choice itself.

intents.message: Three of our trustees roll off next June and nobody's lined up to replace them. Can you help me build a skills matrix for the seats we'll need to fill and a sensible way to approach candidates?
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: No skill in the set covers board composition, succession or trustee recruitment — the governance skill assembles meeting agendas and packets, not the pipeline of who sits on the body.

intents.message: Our social enterprise café is doing well enough that people keep pushing us to open a second site across town. I'm genuinely torn — walk me through the realistic paths, what each one risks, and where you'd land.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour fiscal-sponsorship-entity-advisor is wrong because the mission venture's housing is settled and the live question is expansion — options, risks and a recommendation with no entity, sponsorship or subclassification element.

intents.message: The directors want a recommendation from me before they next sit down, on whether we take over the county meal contract. I'm not asking about how that meeting runs — give me the choices weighed honestly and a line on what would change my mind.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour board-agenda-reporting-builder is wrong because the user disclaims any interest in meeting mechanics and wants the reasoning itself, including the condition that would overturn the recommendation.

intents.message: Three funders open in the same month and we have one writer. I don't want a deadline list — I want the case for each of the three, what we give up by picking one, and how sure you actually are of your pick.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour grant-pipeline-lifecycle-tracker is wrong because the user refuses the deadline-tiered action list and asks instead for tradeoffs, an opportunity cost and a stated confidence level on a single recommended choice.

intents.message: A funder we've courted for years will only come in if we drop the after-school programme. Do we take the money? I want the case both ways, what it costs us either direction, and your actual call — not the application copy.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour grant-loi-proposal-drafter is wrong because the closing clause refuses submission-ready copy and the org has not yet decided whether to accept the funder's condition.

intents.message: We're two years into running the youth workshops under another charity's roof and it's getting awkward — they take a cut and control the bank account. Do we go it alone and set up our own thing, stay put, or is there a middle road?

intents.why: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because, stripped of jargon, the choice is host-charity versus standalone versus hybrid — the housing question the structure specialist owns.

intents.message: A foundation says they'd fund the river cleanup but we haven't got our exemption letter yet, so someone suggested running the money through an established nonprofit instead. What are our options for housing this, and what do we give up under each?
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour grant-loi-proposal-drafter is wrong because no application is being written — the blocker is that the venture has no charitable status and needs a housing arrangement before any money can be received.

intents.why: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because this is deadline-tier triage across live funding entries rather than a framed choice with two to four options and tradeoffs.

intents.why: Nearest neighbour grant-loi-proposal-drafter is wrong because drafting is deferred until the tracked entries are cleaned up; the ask is an audit of unreliable due-date sources and eligibility across the portfolio.

intents.why: Nearest neighbour grantee-responsible-ai-due-diligence-scorecard is wrong because the direction of travel is upward - the organisation authors a single-system conformance memo about itself and sends it to the funder, rather than a funder grading anyone.

intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour ai-governance-assessor is wrong because the gap-and-next-steps language is scoped to one named screener mapped function by function, not to the organisation's overall posture.

intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour ai-incident-response-playbook-builder is wrong because the response plan already exists and the late clause asks for it to be absorbed into a complete four-function crosswalk of one named assistant.

intents.why: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because the speaker sets aside options-and-tradeoffs framing and asks for the responsible-AI questions and red flags to put to each vendor before adopting.

intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour ai-governance-assessor is wrong because the speaker deliberately brackets their own internal posture and asks about adopting a smart feature a vendor is about to switch on.

intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour bias-fairness-reviewer is wrong because the speaker has no access to the system to test and instead needs to judge a selling vendor's fairness claim before any purchase.

intents.message: Two of our program staff want to start on a case-note summarizer a peer organization recommended, and it is a paid subscription. Before I approve the spend I want to know what to look for in how the company uses everything we type into it.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour grantee-responsible-ai-due-diligence-scorecard is wrong because the peer organization is only the source of the tip; the speaker is a buyer weighing a subscription purchase, not a funder scoring another organization.

intents.message: Our per-seat pricing on the volunteer database jumped forty percent at renewal and the contract has an auto-renew clause I missed. What leverage do we actually have to push this supplier back down before the January date?
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: No skill in the set claims this because it is commercial contract and price negotiation on a database with no AI component and no decision framing that any of the twelve descriptions cover.

intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour board-agenda-reporting-builder is wrong because the governance audience is one of three parallel versions of the same facts and nothing formal, such as motions, quorum or a packet, is requested.

intents.message: Take what I've told you about where our grants stand and give me two write-ups off the same facts, a tight one for the board and a plainer one for staff who don't follow funder jargon.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour grant-pipeline-lifecycle-tracker is wrong because the user supplies the funding status themselves and asks only for two audience-pitched renderings of it, not for the status to be assembled or prioritized.

intents.message: Two of our funders and our lead partner each asked how the pilot is going. None of it is a required report and nothing gets submitted anywhere, so I just want one consistent set of write-ups, longer for the partner and tighter for the funders.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour grant-loi-proposal-drafter is wrong because the user rules out any submission and asks for informal, mutually consistent versions for three separate readers.

intents.message: We've already decided to close the Tuesday meal program and that call is made, so please don't re-open it. What I need is how we say it to the board, to the donors who funded it, and to the families who show up, each one honest and consistent with the others.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because the choice is closed and the request is three honest, mutually consistent tellings of it for different audiences.

intents.message: A reporter at the city paper covers homelessness. I'd like a press release announcing our new night shelter plus a short pitch email I could send her, both in her register rather than ours.
intents.label: correctly declined
intents.why: No skill in the set covers media relations, and a press release plus a journalist pitch targets one external channel rather than producing calibrated versions for the organization's own stakeholder groups.

intents.message: Same quarter of work has to go three places this week: the trustees, the program officer at the foundation that covers about a third of our salaries, and the twelve partner orgs in the cohort. The trustees want the risk picture, the program officer will read it against what we said we'd deliver, and the partners mostly want to know what changed for them. One set of facts, three very different letters.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Anthropic's skill covers exec/engineering/cross-functional/customer/board. A program officer reading against stated deliverables is a funder-reporting act with no analogue in that audience set; 'covers a third of our salaries' is restricted-funding context.

intents.message: Our reporting period closed Friday. I need the narrative that goes back to the three restricted grants — each one only wants the piece of the work its own money paid for — plus a plainer version for the whole staff, and something short enough for the newsletter. Nothing can contradict anything else; last year two of them disagreed on a headcount and it was embarrassing.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Restricted-fund segmentation — reporting only the portion each award financed — has no counterpart in a product-management update skill and is the strongest single discriminator in this pair.

intents.message: Write up the last six weeks for two audiences. One is the family foundation that gave us general operating support and reads three paragraphs at most. The other is our community advisory group, who were actually in the room for most of it and will notice if I smooth anything over.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: 'General operating support' is nonprofit finance vocabulary absent from the competitor's entire repo. Community advisory group is a reciprocity audience, not a customer segment.

intents.message: Sprint 14 wrapped. I need the weekly for leadership — RAG status, the two things that slipped and why, and what I need from the platform team. Then a longer cut for the engineers with the actual ticket numbers, and something for the CS folks they can paste to customers who asked about the latency fix.
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: Pure product-management substrate. If the CIL skill fires here it is winning a contest it should lose, and that is a false positive that degrades the whole bundle's measured routing.

intents.message: We're launching Tuesday. I need the internal announcement, the exec one-pager, and the note that goes to the design partners who've been on the beta.
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: Launch-announcement shape, explicitly named in the competitor's own description.

intents.message: Trustees meet in two weeks. I need to build what goes in front of them — what's on the agenda, how long each item gets, which items are just noting and which actually need a vote, and what has to be read beforehand. Two of the items touch a director's other organization so I need that handled properly.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Forward-looking packet construction with time allocation, consent-vs-action classification and a conflict-of-interest handling need. The competitor produces the record afterwards and refuses to proceed without a house minutes format.

intents.message: Put together the papers for the finance committee — the year-to-date against budget, where the restricted balances sit, the two policies due for their annual look, and a short cover note so people actually read it before they turn up.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Packet assembly ahead of a committee sitting; restricted balances is nonprofit fund accounting.

intents.message: I've got the recording and the deck from Thursday's board meeting. Draft the minutes in our house format — resolutions carried, abstentions noted, and the written consent we took by email the week before folded in.
intents.label: correctly declined
intents.why: Retrospective legal-record production. The CIL skill builds the agenda; if it fires on minutes-drafting it is out of scope.

intents.message: Four staff, no IT person, and we've drifted into using AI for intake summaries, the newsletter and some grant drafting. I don't need a per-tool analysis — I need an honest read on whether we as an organization are anywhere near ready for this, and what the first three things to fix are given nobody here has time.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Organization-level maturity with an explicit capacity constraint, and an explicit rejection of the per-system framing the competitor is built around.

intents.message: Board asked me a question I can't answer: are we behind on this compared to organizations our size. Give me something scored, with a path out, that doesn't assume we can hire anyone.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Peer-relative, capacity-tiered scoring. The competitor scores one system against a regime, not an organization against its cohort.

intents.message: We're deploying a CV-screening model in the EU hiring flow. I need this system classified — are we provider or deployer on it, which risk tier it lands in, and what that triggers before it goes live.
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: Per-system role-and-tier classification under a regime CIL's set does not cover. Neither CIL skill should fire; the EU AI Act gap is real and the honest answer is out-of-set.

intents.message: Run the impact assessment on the chatbot before the committee sees it — structured intake, the risk analysis, how it classifies under each regime we're in scope for, and a recommendation with conditions.
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: Single-system impact assessment across regimes — the competitor's exact stated output.

intents.message: Our Texas funder keeps asking whether we follow the federal framework. We run one case-notes tool that matters. Map that tool against the framework properly so I have a memo that stands up, and be explicit about which version you mapped against.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Named framework, single system, memo output, and a version-pinning request — the exact defensive posture the directed NIST revision makes necessary.

intents.message: New guidance dropped last week. Diff it against where our governance posture actually is, flag the gaps, and give me a remediation plan with owners and dates.
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: Regulation-to-posture diff on arbitrary new guidance. CIL's skill crosswalks a system to one named framework; it should not claim general regulatory diffing.

intents.message: A donor-database company is pitching us an AI add-on. I am not technical and we have no lawyer. What do I actually ask them before we sign, and what answers should worry me?
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Buyer-side, pre-contract, explicitly non-technical and unrepresented. The competitor assumes counsel reviewing terms against established governance positions.

intents.message: Here's their DPA and the AI addendum. Review the provisions against our positions — training on our data, liability caps, what happens when they change the underlying model — and flag anything inconsistent with the policy.
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: Document-in-hand contract review against an existing policy — counsel work, not buyer diligence.

intents.message: We've been using a scoring tool to prioritize who gets into the transitional housing program. Someone raised that it seems to push older applicants down. I need this looked at properly — whether it's actually treating people differently and what we do if it is.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Disparate-impact review of a live consequential-decision system against a protected characteristic. Distinct from a whole-system impact assessment.

intents.message: Before we roll the eligibility model out to the other two sites, I want an honest look at whether it lands differently on the people we serve depending on who they are — and I want it anchored to what the law where we operate actually requires, not just a framework.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Carries the re-anchoring signal: statutory duty over framework language. Worth measuring because the description change proposed for this skill is exactly this move.

intents.message: If the intake assistant ever tells a client something wrong about their benefits, I have no idea what we'd do. Who finds out, who calls the client, who decides whether to switch it off, and what we write down. Build us that, sized for an organization with nine people.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Model-harm incident, not a security incident. Every public IR skill found is cyber/SRE, so the boundary is worth measuring even though no first-party competitor exists.

intents.message: We think there's been unauthorized access to the donor database. Walk me through containment, what we're legally required to notify and by when, and the forensics we should preserve.
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: A data-breach response, not an AI incident. The AI-specific framing is the skill's whole claim to novelty and it must not dilute into generic breach handling.

intents.message: We can keep the second site open through spring or close it now and put the money into the one that's working. Board wants my recommendation next month. Lay out the real choices and what would have to be true for each to be right.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Consequential organizational choice with a named decision forum. Generic enough that this pair is the one most likely to expose the skill's trigger surface as too broad.

intents.message: Should we go with Postgres or DynamoDB for the events table? Write it up the way we usually record these so the next engineer knows why.
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: An architecture decision record. Anthropic's `architecture` skill owns this; CIL's should not fire on technical stack choices.

intents.message: Help me think through whether to take the job.
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: Bare personal deliberation carrying two of the skill's own literal trigger phrases and none of its organizational context. The sharpest available test of whether the description is over-broad.

intents.message: The family foundation asked for two pages before they'll invite a full application. We've never worked with them. Draft it — and do not put a single number in there I haven't given you.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Foundation LOI with an explicit claim-accuracy constraint. Community competitors are NIH/NSF/DoD-shaped and assume a federal notice of funding opportunity.

intents.message: Draft the specific aims page and the biosketch for the R01 resubmission, responding to the reviewer critiques from last cycle.
intents.label: correctly declined
intents.why: Federal biomedical research grant. CIL's is foundation philanthropy; the vocabularies do not overlap and neither should the routing.

intents.message: I've lost track of where everything sits. Six funders in play, two of them I think have deadlines this month but I'm not certain and I don't want to trust my own note — and one I may have already missed. Get me straight on what's actually live and what's next.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Multi-funder pipeline state with an explicit deadline-source-verification signal, which is the skill's distinguishing discipline.

intents.message: We fund about forty small organizations and several have started using AI in their programs. I need a consistent way to understand where each of them actually is, without it turning into a compliance burden that punishes the three-person shops for being three-person shops.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Funder-side, portfolio-wide, with the capacity-asymmetry concern stated by the user. Note for the design review: this prompt is also the argument for the no-composite-score rule.

intents.message: Four of us have been running this as a project under another nonprofit's umbrella for two years. It's outgrown that. I want to understand what the actual options are — stay, move to a different arrangement, or stand something up ourselves — and what each would mean.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Entity-structure deliberation framed as options rather than advice. Zero public equivalents found; these cases protect the boundary rather than contest an incumbent.

intents.message: We're registering an association in Lomé and I need to know how the ministry accord works and what it means for receiving European money.
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: Non-US jurisdiction where the US fiscal-sponsorship instrument does not exist. Confidently recommending a US structure here is the highest-harm failure mode identified in the board review — this case makes it measurable.

One set of facts, three very different letters.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Anthropic's skill covers exec/engineering/cross-functional/customer/board. A program officer reading against stated deliverables is a funder-reporting act with no analogue in that audience set; 'covers a third of our salaries' is restricted-funding context.

intents.message: Our reporting period closed Friday. I need the narrative that goes back to the three restricted grants — each one only wants the piece of the work its own money paid for — plus a plainer version for the whole staff, and something short enough for the newsletter. Nothing can contradict anything else; last year two of them disagreed on a headcount and it was embarrassing.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Restricted-fund segmentation — reporting only the portion each award financed — has no counterpart in a product-management update skill and is the strongest single discriminator in this pair.

intents.message: Write up the last six weeks for two audiences. One is the family foundation that gave us general operating support and reads three paragraphs at most. The other is our community advisory group, who were actually in the room for most of it and will notice if I smooth anything over.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: 'General operating support' is nonprofit finance vocabulary absent from the competitor's entire repo. Community advisory group is a reciprocity audience, not a customer segment.

intents.message: Sprint 14 wrapped. I need the weekly for leadership — RAG status, the two things that slipped and why, and what I need from the platform team. Then a longer cut for the engineers with the actual ticket numbers, and something for the CS folks they can paste to customers who asked about the latency fix.
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: Pure product-management substrate. If the CIL skill fires here it is winning a contest it should lose, and that is a false positive that degrades the whole bundle's measured routing.

intents.message: We're launching Tuesday. I need the internal announcement, the exec one-pager, and the note that goes to the design partners who've been on the beta.
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: Launch-announcement shape, explicitly named in the competitor's own description.

intents.message: Trustees meet in two weeks. I need to build what goes in front of them — what's on the agenda, how long each item gets, which items are just noting and which actually need a vote, and what has to be read beforehand. Two of the items touch a director's other organization so I need that handled properly.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Forward-looking packet construction with time allocation, consent-vs-action classification and a conflict-of-interest handling need. The competitor produces the record afterwards and refuses to proceed without a house minutes format.

intents.message: Put together the papers for the finance committee — the year-to-date against budget, where the restricted balances sit, the two policies due for their annual look, and a short cover note so people actually read it before they turn up.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Packet assembly ahead of a committee sitting; restricted balances is nonprofit fund accounting.

intents.message: I've got the recording and the deck from Thursday's board meeting. Draft the minutes in our house format — resolutions carried, abstentions noted, and the written consent we took by email the week before folded in.
intents.label: correctly declined
intents.why: Retrospective legal-record production. The CIL skill builds the agenda; if it fires on minutes-drafting it is out of scope.

intents.message: Four staff, no IT person, and we've drifted into using AI for intake summaries, the newsletter and some grant drafting. I don't need a per-tool analysis — I need an honest read on whether we as an organization are anywhere near ready for this, and what the first three things to fix are given nobody here has time.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Organization-level maturity with an explicit capacity constraint, and an explicit rejection of the per-system framing the competitor is built around.

intents.message: Board asked me a question I can't answer: are we behind on this compared to organizations our size. Give me something scored, with a path out, that doesn't assume we can hire anyone.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Peer-relative, capacity-tiered scoring. The competitor scores one system against a regime, not an organization against its cohort.

intents.message: We're deploying a CV-screening model in the EU hiring flow. I need this system classified — are we provider or deployer on it, which risk tier it lands in, and what that triggers before it goes live.
intents.label: correctly declined
intents.why: Per-system role-and-tier classification under a regime CIL's set does not cover. Neither CIL skill should fire; the EU AI Act gap is real and the honest answer is out-of-set.

intents.message: Run the impact assessment on the chatbot before the committee sees it — structured intake, the risk analysis, how it classifies under each regime we're in scope for, and a recommendation with conditions.
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: Single-system impact assessment across regimes — the competitor's exact stated output.

intents.message: Our Texas funder keeps asking whether we follow the federal framework. We run one case-notes tool that matters. Map that tool against the framework properly so I have a memo that stands up, and be explicit about which version you mapped against.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Named framework, single system, memo output, and a version-pinning request — the exact defensive posture the directed NIST revision makes necessary.

intents.message: New guidance dropped last week. Diff it against where our governance posture actually is, flag the gaps, and give me a remediation plan with owners and dates.
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: Regulation-to-posture diff on arbitrary new guidance. CIL's skill crosswalks a system to one named framework; it should not claim general regulatory diffing.

intents.message: A donor-database company is pitching us an AI add-on. I am not technical and we have no lawyer. What do I actually ask them before we sign, and what answers should worry me?
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Buyer-side, pre-contract, explicitly non-technical and unrepresented. The competitor assumes counsel reviewing terms against established governance positions.

intents.message: Here's their DPA and the AI addendum. Review the provisions against our positions — training on our data, liability caps, what happens when they change the underlying model — and flag anything inconsistent with the policy.
intents.label: correctly declined
intents.why: Document-in-hand contract review against an existing policy — counsel work, not buyer diligence.

intents.message: We've been using a scoring tool to prioritize who gets into the transitional housing program. Someone raised that it seems to push older applicants down. I need this looked at properly — whether it's actually treating people differently and what we do if it is.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Disparate-impact review of a live consequential-decision system against a protected characteristic. Distinct from a whole-system impact assessment.

intents.message: Before we roll the eligibility model out to the other two sites, I want an honest look at whether it lands differently on the people we serve depending on who they are — and I want it anchored to what the law where we operate actually requires, not just a framework.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Carries the re-anchoring signal: statutory duty over framework language. Worth measuring because the description change proposed for this skill is exactly this move.

intents.message: If the intake assistant ever tells a client something wrong about their benefits, I have no idea what we'd do. Who finds out, who calls the client, who decides whether to switch it off, and what we write down. Build us that, sized for an organization with nine people.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Model-harm incident, not a security incident. Every public IR skill found is cyber/SRE, so the boundary is worth measuring even though no first-party competitor exists.

intents.message: We think there's been unauthorized access to the donor database. Walk me through containment, what we're legally required to notify and by when, and the forensics we should preserve.
intents.label: correctly declined
intents.why: A data-breach response, not an AI incident. The AI-specific framing is the skill's whole claim to novelty and it must not dilute into generic breach handling.

intents.message: We can keep the second site open through spring or close it now and put the money into the one that's working. Board wants my recommendation next month. Lay out the real choices and what would have to be true for each to be right.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Consequential organizational choice with a named decision forum. Generic enough that this pair is the one most likely to expose the skill's trigger surface as too broad.

intents.message: Should we go with Postgres or DynamoDB for the events table? Write it up the way we usually record these so the next engineer knows why.
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: An architecture decision record. Anthropic's `architecture` skill owns this; CIL's should not fire on technical stack choices.

intents.message: Help me think through whether to take the job.
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: Bare personal deliberation carrying two of the skill's own literal trigger phrases and none of its organizational context. The sharpest available test of whether the description is over-broad.

intents.message: The family foundation asked for two pages before they'll invite a full application. We've never worked with them. Draft it — and do not put a single number in there I haven't given you.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Foundation LOI with an explicit claim-accuracy constraint. Community competitors are NIH/NSF/DoD-shaped and assume a federal notice of funding opportunity.

intents.message: Draft the specific aims page and the biosketch for the R01 resubmission, responding to the reviewer critiques from last cycle.
intents.label: correctly declined
intents.why: Federal biomedical research grant. CIL's is foundation philanthropy; the vocabularies do not overlap and neither should the routing.

intents.message: I've lost track of where everything sits. Six funders in play, two of them I think have deadlines this month but I'm not certain and I don't want to trust my own note — and one I may have already missed. Get me straight on what's actually live and what's next.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Multi-funder pipeline state with an explicit deadline-source-verification signal, which is the skill's distinguishing discipline.

intents.message: We fund about forty small organizations and several have started using AI in their programs. I need a consistent way to understand where each of them actually is, without it turning into a compliance burden that punishes the three-person shops for being three-person shops.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Funder-side, portfolio-wide, with the capacity-asymmetry concern stated by the user. Note for the design review: this prompt is also the argument for the no-composite-score rule.

intents.message: Four of us have been running this as a project under another nonprofit's umbrella for two years. It's outgrown that. I want to understand what the actual options are — stay, move to a different arrangement, or stand something up ourselves — and what each would mean.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Entity-structure deliberation framed as options rather than advice. Zero public equivalents found; these cases protect the boundary rather than contest an incumbent.

intents.message: We're registering an association in Lomé and I need to know how the ministry accord works and what it means for receiving European money.
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: Non-US jurisdiction where the US fiscal-sponsorship instrument does not exist. Confidently recommending a US structure here is the highest-harm failure mode identified in the board review — this case makes it measurable.

variants.name: model
variants.how: the model planner chooses a skill by reading the skills' descriptions

intents.message: A funder asked whether we follow the federal AI risk framework. Before I answer I want an honest scored read across everything - oversight, documentation, data handling, how we'd cope with a failure - since we run about a dozen AI tools and no single one is the question.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour nist-ai-rmf-crosswalk-generator is wrong because the framework reference is only the prompt for the ask, while the request itself names no single system and demands a scored read spanning every governance dimension at once.

intents.message: We're a small family foundation and we've started leaning on AI inside our own grantmaking workflow. Someone suggested we score this the way we'd score a grantee, but I need it turned inward - how does our own house rate across the governance dimensions?
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour grantee-responsible-ai-due-diligence-scorecard is wrong because the funder is deliberately pointing the assessment at its own internal AI use rather than at any grantee's.

intents.message: We already signed up for three AI tools last year without much thought - one of them we barely use - and now they're baked into our case notes and donor letters. I don't need help picking a vendor, I need someone to grade how badly we're running what we already have.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour responsible-ai-procurement-checklist is wrong because the purchase already happened and the tools are in production, so the ask is a maturity read on deployed systems rather than pre-purchase vendor vetting.

intents.message: Last quarter our AI assistant leaked a client's address in a mass email and we handled it - the containment steps and the apology all went out fine. What I want now, and this is the part I keep putting off, is a scored read on every dimension of how we run AI, not another response plan.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour ai-incident-response-playbook-builder is wrong because the incident is already closed out and the late clause rejects a further response plan in favour of a scored read across every governance dimension.

intents.message: We have nothing written down about staff using AI. Can you draft us an actual acceptable-use policy from scratch - which tools are allowed, what data can never go into them, who signs off on exceptions - something I can drop straight into the staff handbook?
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: No skill in the set drafts governing policy text from scratch - the assessor explicitly disclaims policy drafting and hands it to a policy builder that is absent from these twelve, and every other skill assesses, scores, tracks, or reports rather than authoring an internal rule set.

intents.message: We just finished a maturity review of every AI tool we run and the weakest score by far was what happens when something goes wrong. Do not re-score us. Write the actual step-by-step for who gets called, how we rank how bad it is, and what we tell the family affected.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour ai-governance-assessor is wrong because the scoring pass is already done and the speaker explicitly refuses another one, asking instead for the standing response procedure that closes the identified gap.

intents.message: When our AI scheduling assistant leaked two clients' phone numbers into the wrong thread, I improvised notes to the clients, the board and our main funder in one afternoon. I never want to improvise that again, so turn the whole sequence into a documented process with severity levels.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour stakeholder-update-generator is wrong because the multi-audience notes are the past improvisation being replaced, and the deliverable named late in the request is a documented severity-tiered process.

intents.message: Our donor CRM's AI assistant was down for eleven hours during the year-end campaign and nobody knew who was supposed to decide whether to keep sending appeals by hand. We are staying with the supplier; I just want the internal steps we follow the next time a tool like this drops out.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour responsible-ai-procurement-checklist is wrong because the speaker rules out re-evaluating the supplier and wants internal containment and decision steps for a future outage of a critical AI-dependent workflow.

intents.message: Our conformance memo flagged that we have nothing written down for the moment one of our models produces something harmful. Rather than redo the mapping, I want the document that tells a staffer at nine at night who to call, how bad it counts as, and how we tell the person harmed.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour nist-ai-rmf-crosswalk-generator is wrong because the speaker declines to redo a framework mapping and asks for the operational runbook content, triage, severity and disclosure, that the memo found missing.

intents.message: A volunteer clicked a phishing link last week and someone used our payroll portal to reroute two staff direct deposits. What do we need to do now to lock the account down and meet our reporting obligations?
intents.label: should have declined
intents.why: No skill in the set claims this because it is a conventional payroll-fraud and phishing incident with no AI system involved, and the library's incident skill is scoped exclusively to AI failures and harms.

intents.message: Our scholarship shortlisting model has been running a year now. Applicants who declare a disability seem to drop out at the shortlist step far more often than everyone else - can you work out whether that gap is real and what we should document about it?
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour ai-governance-assessor is wrong because the ask is an outcome-rate comparison on one named shortlisting model against a protected attribute, not a read on whether fairness practices exist anywhere.

intents.message: My data guy says we have to pick between equal selection rates and equal error rates for the housing waitlist model, and I honestly don't know how to choose. Can you work that through on the actual model and show me which groups come out worse under each option?
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because the choice is specifically between fairness metrics and must be settled by running them on one named waitlist model to see which groups fare worse, not by a general options-and-tradeoffs brief.

intents.message: We licensed a resume-screening product last spring - the vendor due diligence was done back then and the contract is signed. Six months of our own hiring data later, I want it checked against our applicants: are women and older candidates advancing at lower rates through it?
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour responsible-ai-procurement-checklist is wrong because the purchase and vendor check are finished, and the ask is an outcome-rate test of the live screener on the organisation's own applicants by gender and age.

intents.message: Somebody on staff complained that the food-pantry eligibility tool turned a family away unfairly, and yes, we logged it and apologised already. The complaint is one case though - what I want is that tool run against our whole year of decisions to see if Spanish-speaking households come out worse.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour ai-incident-response-playbook-builder is wrong because the single complaint is already handled and the late clause asks for a population-level outcome comparison on one named eligibility tool by language group.

intents.message: Our board approved one new hire to own AI oversight and ethics across the organisation. I need a job description and a short interview rubric for the role, plus a sensible salary band for a mid-size nonprofit - can you draft those by Friday?
intents.label: correctly declined
intents.why: No skill in the set produces recruiting artefacts - job descriptions, interview rubrics and compensation bands are HR work, and the AI subject matter of the role does not turn the request into an assessment, a fairness test, or a board packet.

intents.message: Trustees meet a week from Thursday and I normally just circulate a written progress recap, but this time I need the real thing — timed sections with a presenter for each, year-to-date financials, and two items going to a vote where our treasurer has to step out.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour stakeholder-update-generator is wrong because the user explicitly sets aside the circulated recap in favour of one formal internal sitting carrying financials, timed presenters and a recusal-affected vote.

intents.message: Most of next month's trustee meeting is about where we stand with funders. Lay the meeting out for me — running order, time per block, who owns each, pre-reads to send ahead — and note that two applications need directors' approval before we submit.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour grant-pipeline-lifecycle-tracker is wrong because funding is merely the subject matter of a meeting whose structure — timings, owners, pre-reads and a sign-off item — is the actual deliverable.

intents.message: One of our directors owns the firm we're about to sign a lease with. How do I sequence Tuesday's meeting so her stepping out is on the record and the rest still have the numbers to carry the vote?
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour fiscal-sponsorship-entity-advisor is wrong because the user is not asking whether the dual role is defensible or for anything in writing, only how to order the meeting so the recusal is minuted and the remaining directors still make quorum.

intents.message: Our exec committee is chewing over whether to merge the two program teams and everyone has a view. Before we get there, map the ninety minutes for me — order, owners, and the exact wording of what they'll be asked to adopt at the end.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because the merger question is only the topic; the late detail asks for the time map and the resolution wording, which is the meeting's structure rather than the choice itself.

intents.message: Three of our trustees roll off next June and nobody's lined up to replace them. Can you help me build a skills matrix for the seats we'll need to fill and a sensible way to approach candidates?
intents.label: correctly declined
intents.why: No skill in the set covers board composition, succession or trustee recruitment — the governance skill assembles meeting agendas and packets, not the pipeline of who sits on the body.

intents.message: Our social enterprise café is doing well enough that people keep pushing us to open a second site across town. I'm genuinely torn — walk me through the realistic paths, what each one risks, and where you'd land.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour fiscal-sponsorship-entity-advisor is wrong because the mission venture's housing is settled and the live question is expansion — options, risks and a recommendation with no entity, sponsorship or subclassification element.

intents.message: The directors want a recommendation from me before they next sit down, on whether we take over the county meal contract. I'm not asking about how that meeting runs — give me the choices weighed honestly and a line on what would change my mind.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour board-agenda-reporting-builder is wrong because the user disclaims any interest in meeting mechanics and wants the reasoning itself, including the condition that would overturn the recommendation.

intents.message: Three funders open in the same month and we have one writer. I don't want a deadline list — I want the case for each of the three, what we give up by picking one, and how sure you actually are of your pick.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour grant-pipeline-lifecycle-tracker is wrong because the user refuses the deadline-tiered action list and asks instead for tradeoffs, an opportunity cost and a stated confidence level on a single recommended choice.

intents.message: A funder we've courted for years will only come in if we drop the after-school programme. Do we take the money? I want the case both ways, what it costs us either direction, and your actual call — not the application copy.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour grant-loi-proposal-drafter is wrong because the closing clause refuses submission-ready copy and the org has not yet decided whether to accept the funder's condition.

intents.message: We closed the west site eighteen months ago and it was clearly the wrong call. There's no new decision on the table — I want an honest look back at how we got there so the leadership team doesn't repeat it.
intents.label: correctly declined
intents.why: No skill in the set covers a retrospective on a decision already taken — the decision skill is explicitly pre-decision and the only post-mortem capability in the set is scoped to AI incidents.

intents.message: We're two years into running the youth workshops under another charity's roof and it's getting awkward — they take a cut and control the bank account. Do we go it alone and set up our own thing, stay put, or is there a middle road?
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because, stripped of jargon, the choice is host-charity versus standalone versus hybrid — the housing question the structure specialist owns.

intents.message: A foundation says they'd fund the river cleanup but we haven't got our exemption letter yet, so someone suggested running the money through an established nonprofit instead. What are our options for housing this, and what do we give up under each?
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour grant-loi-proposal-drafter is wrong because no application is being written — the blocker is that the venture has no charitable status and needs a housing arrangement before any money can be received.

intents.message: Half our grant money still lands in our sponsor's account and half in ours now that we have our own letter. Before I clean up the funding side, I need to know whether we should be leaving that sponsor at all and what unwinding it would involve.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour grant-pipeline-lifecycle-tracker is wrong because the grants are only the symptom and the user defers them explicitly in favour of deciding whether to exit the sponsorship arrangement.

intents.message: Our congregation wants to open a coffee shop that hires women coming out of trafficking. The elders want the profits feeding the ministry, but nobody wants the church's tax-exempt status anywhere near a trading business — what are the sensible ways to set this up?
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because the late clause makes this a question about how a trading venture relates to an exempt church body, which is a structure choice rather than an open strategic option set.

intents.message: Our auditor flagged that we've never adopted a whistleblower policy. Can you draft one for us — how someone reports concerns, protection from retaliation, and who's meant to investigate?
intents.label: correctly declined
intents.why: No skill in the set drafts whistleblower or retaliation-protection policies — the structure specialist's policy work is confined to entity, sponsorship and conflicting-role questions, and no general nonprofit policy drafter exists here.

intents.message: Three funders close inside the same week but Hollings is the one we are actually submitting. I still have nothing written for the section on who we serve or how we would know it worked - can you draft both at 400 words?
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour grant-pipeline-lifecycle-tracker is wrong because the competing deadlines are already resolved by the user's own choice, leaving two named sections of copy at a fixed word count for one funder.

intents.message: We're applying through our fiscal sponsor and the application has a whole box asking how the money would flow and who is legally accountable. We settled that arrangement last year, so I just need those two paragraphs written for the box.
intents.label: chose its sibling
intents.why: Nearest neighbour fiscal-sponsorship-entity-advisor is wrong because the sponsorship structure is already decided and the ask is application prose describing it, not guidance on what the arrangement should be.

intents.message: The Merriweather giving office says they want to hear what we've been up to, but it arrived as four questions with a 500-word cap on each. Write our answers: who we serve, what we'd do with the funds, and how we'd know it worked.
intents.label: chose nothing
intents.why: Nearest neighbour stakeholder-update-generator is wrong because the capped answer boxes and the forward-looking use-of-funds question mark this as one funder's application copy rather than a recap circulated to several audiences.

intents.message: This funder's application now asks how we oversee any AI we use in our programs. I don't need a rubric or an audit of ourselves, I need our answer written into their 300-word box by next week.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour grantee-responsible-ai-due-diligence-scorecard is wrong because the user is the applicant drafting a word-capped answer inside a funder's form, not a funder scoring anyone's AI maturity.

intents.message: I want to write a personal ask to the handful of individuals who each gave us ten thousand dollars last year, a warm letter over my signature for our year-end appeal rather than anything institutional.
intents.label: correctly declined
intents.why: No skill in the set covers individual major-donor solicitation or year-end appeal letters, which are neither a funder application, a portfolio status view, nor a multi-audience digest of recent activity.

intents.message: Before I talk to anybody I need the funding picture straight in my own head: which ones are still alive, which are dead, and what I personally have to move on this week.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour stakeholder-update-generator is wrong because the only reader is the user, and what is wanted is a live-versus-dead status classification plus a personal action list rather than versions for other audiences.

intents.message: Five funders are open to us this fall and realistically we can get two out the door. Rank them by what closes first and where we already have a warm contact, then tell me which two to chase.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because this is deadline-tier triage across live funding entries rather than a framed choice with two to four options and tradeoffs.

intents.message: Half the due dates in my funding sheet came off a newsletter and I am not sure we even qualify for three of them. Before I start writing anything for anyone, sort out which dates are real, which ones we are eligible for, and what is about to slip past me.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour grant-loi-proposal-drafter is wrong because drafting is deferred until the tracked entries are cleaned up; the ask is an audit of unreliable due-date sources and eligibility across the portfolio.

intents.message: My co-director wants me to brief her and the team on the money situation. Honestly I can't tell anyone anything until I have my own ranked list of what is about to close and which applications are stuck, so do that first.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour stakeholder-update-generator is wrong because the requested artifact, arriving at the end of the message, is a ranked internal view of stalled and closing entries that the user needs before any audience version could be written.

intents.message: Our auditor says our federal drawdowns don't tie out to the general ledger for the last two quarters. How do I reconcile them, and what do I need ready before single audit fieldwork starts?
intents.label: correctly declined
intents.why: No skill in the set handles grant financial reconciliation or single-audit preparation, which is accounting and compliance work rather than pipeline tracking, drafting, or reporting to audiences.

intents.message: Three of the nonprofits we fund just adopted a vendor's AI case-management tool, and our renewal decisions land in November. I need a light-touch way to rate how responsibly each organization handles it, without burying a two-person team in enterprise paperwork.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour responsible-ai-procurement-checklist is wrong because the speaker is a funder rating the practices of organizations it already funds rather than a buyer deciding whether to purchase the tool.

intents.message: An applicant's proposal claims their tutoring chatbot follows the federal AI risk framework and ISO 42001. I don't need a function-by-function mapping of their system, I need a rubric to weigh that claim fairly against the other applications in this round.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour nist-ai-rmf-crosswalk-generator is wrong because the speaker explicitly declines a single-system framework mapping and wants a comparative scoring rubric applied to competing applicants.

intents.message: One of our grantees uses an algorithm to decide which families get housing vouchers first. I am in no position to run a disparate-impact test on their model, but at the next site visit I need a consistent way to grade how they oversee and document it against the rest of the cohort.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour bias-fairness-reviewer is wrong because the speaker rules out testing the model for outcome disparities and instead wants comparable governance grading of a funded organization.

intents.message: Our trustees keep asking whether careful AI practices should become a written requirement in our grant agreements. I would rather skip the options memo, though, because what I actually need is the instrument we would use to grade each organization we support.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because the speaker waves off the options-and-tradeoffs framing and asks, late in the request, for the grading instrument a funder would apply to the organizations it supports.

intents.message: Before we release the second tranche to any organization we support, I want a standard set of asks covering audited financials, insurance certificates and board minutes. Nothing technological about it, just the paperwork side of whether they can absorb the money.
intents.label: should have declined

intents.message: Trustees meet in two weeks. intents.why: Forward-looking packet construction with time allocation, consent-vs-action classification and a conflict-of-interest handling need. The competitor produces the record afterwards and refuses to proceed without a house minutes format.

intents.message: We're deploying a CV-screening model in the EU hiring flow. I need this system classified — are we provider or deployer on it, which risk tier it lands in, and what that triggers before it goes live.

intents.message: Run the impact assessment on the chatbot before the committee sees it — structured intake, the risk analysis, how it classifies under each regime we're in scope for, and a recommendation with conditions.
intents.label: correctly declined
intents.why: Single-system impact assessment across regimes — the competitor's exact stated output.

intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Named framework, single system, memo output, and a version-pinning request — the exact defensive posture the directed NIST revision makes necessary.

intents.why: Buyer-side, pre-contract, explicitly non-technical and unrepresented. The competitor assumes counsel reviewing terms against established governance positions.

intents.message: Here's their DPA and the AI addendum. Review the provisions against our positions — training on our data, liability caps, what happens when they change the underlying model — and flag anything inconsistent with the policy.
intents.label: correctly declined

intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Consequential organizational choice with a named decision forum. Generic enough that this pair is the one most likely to expose the skill's trigger surface as too broad.

intents.message: Should we go with Postgres or DynamoDB for the events table? Write it up the way we usually record these so the next engineer knows why.
intents.label: correctly declined
intents.why: An architecture decision record. Anthropic's `architecture` skill owns this; CIL's should not fire on technical stack choices.

intents.message: Help me think through whether to take the job.
intents.label: correctly declined
intents.why: Bare personal deliberation carrying two of the skill's own literal trigger phrases and none of its organizational context. The sharpest available test of whether the description is over-broad.

intents.message: The family foundation asked for two pages before they'll invite a full application. We've never worked with them. Draft it — and do not put a single number in there I haven't given you.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Foundation LOI with an explicit claim-accuracy constraint. Community competitors are NIH/NSF/DoD-shaped and assume a federal notice of funding opportunity.

intents.message: Draft the specific aims page and the biosketch for the R01 resubmission, responding to the reviewer critiques from last cycle.
intents.label: correctly declined
intents.why: Federal biomedical research grant. CIL's is foundation philanthropy; the vocabularies do not overlap and neither should the routing.

intents.message: I've lost track of where everything sits. Six funders in play, two of them I think have deadlines this month but I'm not certain and I don't want to trust my own note — and one I may have already missed. Get me straight on what's actually live and what's next.
intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Multi-funder pipeline state with an explicit deadline-source-verification signal, which is the skill's distinguishing discipline.

intents.message: We fund about forty small organizations and several have started using AI in their programs. I need a consistent way to understand where each of them actually is, without it turning into a compliance burden that punishes the three-person shops for being three-person shops.

intents.label: right skill
intents.why: Entity-structure deliberation framed as options rather than advice. Zero public equivalents found; these cases protect the boundary rather than contest an incumbent.

intents.message: We're registering an association in Lomé and I need to know how the ministry accord works and what it means for receiving European money.
intents.label: correctly declined
intents.why: Non-US jurisdiction where the US fiscal-sponsorship instrument does not exist. Confidently recommending a US structure here is the highest-harm failure mode identified in the board review — this case makes it measurable.
